To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of the interventions were primary, skills based, and used individual and group interventions.

1) the most recent literature on workplace interventions is dominated by primary and secondary preventive interventions, 2) skills training is the most common intervention, 3) the most common combination of intervention levels is individual, group and organizational, and 4), the most frequent support of interventions is psychosocial intervention and/or participatory research.

The most effective preventive psychological interventions in the workplace are skills training interventions that include a combination of individual-, group-, and organizational-level interventions, and that are supported by psychosocio-logical intervention or participatory action research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effectiveness of primary and secondary interventions in the workplace.
the development and evaluation of primary and secondary preventive interventions for workers in organizations.
identifying the best practices of preventive psychological interventions in organizations and the outcomes associated with them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a need for a more comprehensive understanding of the complexity of the workplace, the nature of the intervention and its outcomes, and how to integrate these components in order to improve the effectiveness of preventive interventions.
the workplace interventions that are based on Cottrell's model have a positive effect on workers.
the workplace interventions that are most effective for mental health are the ones that are multi-level, comprehensive, and integrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the workplace prevention interventions are still in their infancy.
the majority of studies were successful in improving work and mental health-related outcomes.
the literature on preventive interventions in the workplace has grown and evolved in the last five years, and there are still significant gaps in the literature that require more research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the workplace is the best place to intervene.
there is a need for a more comprehensive approach to workplace interventions, one that includes the organization, workers, and their work.
there are a number of promising workplace interventions that can have a positive impact on both work and mental health.
